rationale: No-spec round: there is no story/spec, so acceptance never ran and confidence is low; the edge-case lens ran and the standards audit passed with no coverage gap. 2 blocking findings: isResponsesOnlyGpt sends Responses-only GPT ids that are not in the table to chat-completions (CR-002), and blank/whitespace catalog ids get through as VS Code models (CR-001, reachability not confirmed). 1 deferred (known-family table values override the tenant's features.tools/multimodal flags; this predates the change) -> code-review-deferred.md; 2 dismissed (non-chat deployments: embeddings use a separate endpoint; listing every tenant variant is what the task asks for).

standards_review.notes: 4 commits all follow Conventional Commits format: docs(proxy), fix(proxy), feat(proxy), feat(proxy). All have <type>(<scope>): <subject> structure within 100 char limit.

All imports include .js extensions per code-quality.md. No console.log or require() detected. Proper type annotations on exports (TenantModelDescriptor, VsCodeCapabilityEntry, WriteVsCodeConfigResult, etc.). Error handling uses ConfigurationError. Functions under 50 lines except utility functions. No hardcoded secrets or unsafe patterns.

Credentials (gatewayKey) passed in Authorization headers, not logged. All logging uses sanitizeLogArgs() to redact sensitive parameters (gatewayKey, proxyUrl treated as inferenceGatewayApiKey/inferenceGatewayBaseUrl). No hardcoded secrets. findings.title: Blank catalog ids become VS Code models
findings.problem: parseCatalogResponseDescriptors only checks typeof id === 'string'. extractModelId returns '' when id and base_name are falsy and deployment_name is '', and a whitespace-only id is truthy, so both pass the filter untrimmed.
findings.impact: A model with an empty or whitespace id and name is written to chatLanguageModels.json and shown in the VS Code picker, and it cannot serve requests. Before this change only table-matched ids were written, so the path is new. Reachability is unconfirmed: it depends on the live /v1/llm_models data containing such an entry.
findings.recommendation: Trim the extracted id and skip empty results: const id = extractModelId(model)?.trim(); if (!id || model.enabled === false || seen.has(id)) continue;

findings.title: Responses-only GPT ids routed to chat-completions
findings.problem: isResponsesOnlyGpt marks an unknown id as Responses-only only when its GPT major is 6 or higher, and it strips only the 'openai.' prefix. Untabled 5.x Responses deployments fall through to apiType chat-completions with no zero data retention. Examples: gpt-5.1-codex, gpt-5.6-nova, a gpt-5.5+ variant the resolver does not match, or a GPT-6 id with another vendor prefix such as azure.gpt-6-sol. This contradicts the table (gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.6-* are responses) and opencode-dynamic-models.ts, which records gpt-5.1-codex, gpt-5.2-*, gpt-5.4-* and 5.5/5.6 CodeMie deployments as Responses-API-only.
findings.impact: Every tenant model in these families is now listed, so VS Code offers these deployments with the wrong endpoint (/v1/chat/completions), and every request to them fails. Before this change they were not listed at all.
findings.recommendation: Make the default detection match the repo's known Responses families: parse major and minor and treat major > 5 or (major === 5 && minor >= 5) as responses, plus codex variants. Strip any vendor prefix (e.g. /^[a-z_]+[./]/) instead of only 'openai.'. Consider sharing the RESPONSES_API_MODEL_PATTERNS list from opencode-dynamic-models.ts.
